audit_findings.title: The merger perimeter is reversed: IMXI equity is extinguished, not enlarged
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.00 per share contractual cash consideration versus $1.67-$2.76 per share DCF values, a $13.24-$14.33 per share difference
audit_findings.mechanism: Replaces the standalone OE perpetuity with a merger-closing cash claim; standalone OE, growth, shares and bridge apply only to a failure outcome.
audit_findings.evidence: The Merger Agreement provides that each share of the Company’s common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the Merger (subject to limited exceptions such as treasury shares or shares as to which dissenters’ rights have been properly exercised in accordance with Delaware law ) will be cancelled and converted into the right to receive $16.00 per share in cash, without interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error. The filings identify IMXI as the target and state that its outstanding common shares will be cancelled for $16.00 cash at closing. Treating the merger as growth of IMXI's public-equity perimeter produces the wrong valued claim and a conclusion far below the contractual consideration, although closing remains conditional.
audit_findings.action: Confirm closing status as of the valuation date and rerun an outcome tree covering $16.00 closing consideration, closing timing, failure value, $27.3 million reverse termination fee, $19.8 million company termination fee where applicable, and treatment of outstanding awards.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include regulated operating float
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $150.636 million, or $4.71 per fully diluted share; exact non-distributable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the cash-and-short-term-investment bridge add-back to the amount demonstrably distributable after settlement and regulatory liquidity requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to applicable licensing laws, certain domestic and foreign subsidiaries of the Company are required to maintain minimum tangible net worth and liquid assets (eligible securities) to cover the amount outstanding of wire transfers and money orders payable.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated misclassification. The filing establishes that subsidiaries must maintain eligible liquid assets against payment obligations, but does not quantify how much of the $150.636 million is trapped. Because the entire add-back exceeds every reported scenario equity value of $53-$88 million, even a partial restriction is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 30, 2026 cash balance to jurisdictional eligible-securities requirements, the $85.007 million wire-transfer and money-order payable balance, $16.130 million prepaid wires, $99.744 million net receivables, settlement timing and other required operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The negative anchor may capitalize merger costs as a perpetual operating burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.464 million FY2025 transaction costs, versus the negative $6.2 million OE anchor; also $3.286 million settlement gain and $0.742 million restructuring costs require consistent treatment
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes normalized anchor OE and therefore every forecast year, terminal value and operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: Transaction costs for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 amounted to $ 10.5 million, $ 1.8 million and $ 0.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved normalization issue. The filed transaction cost alone equals 169% of the negative OE anchor and, if retained as recurring, could turn a temporary merger-related expense into a perpetual burden. Its gross amount is sufficient to change the anchor's sign before tax and other adjustments, but the supplied record does not show the owner-earnings bridge needed to prove the actual error.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2025 OE from net income through noncash items, capital expenditure, working capital and taxes; identify whether the $10.464 million transaction cost, $3.286 million gain, $0.742 million restructuring cost and related tax effects were retained, excluded or double-counted, then rerun all scenarios with a consistently normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: Short-cycle settlement balances may be mistaken for durable reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 cash-flow effects of negative $7.053 million from receivables, negative $7.405 million from prepaid wires and positive $0.036 million from wire-transfer payables, net negative $14.422 million; first-half 2026 prepaid-wires effect reversed to positive $43.385 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes the working-capital component of anchor OE by separating transient settlement timing from durable operating reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: Accounts receivable are recorded upon initiation of the wire transfer and are typically due to the Company within five days.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification issue, but the filed movements are material relative to the negative $6.2 million anchor. The rapid reversal in prepaid-wire cash flow supports a timing concern, and the identified FY2025 settlement movements alone exceed twice the anchor loss. The record does not establish that the valuation used these exact amounts or what normalized level is appropriate.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the FY2025 working-capital adjustment from monthly or quarterly average receivables, prepaid wires and matching payment liabilities; reconcile it to the FY2025 and first-half 2026 cash-flow statements and rerun OE using normalized settlement balances.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor predates a specified 2026 demand shock
audit_findings.magnitude: first-half 2026 revenue fell $52.329 million, or 17.1%, transaction volume and principal sent each fell approximately 12.0%, and adjusted EBITDA fell $20.668 million, or 41.0%, versus first-half 2025; tax-specific effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes normalized OE and potentially the near-term growth and margin path used in the scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, taxes imposed on the money transfer industry such as the 1% excise tax on cash remittances originated in the United States, effective in 2026, may result in a lower volume of money transfers, which could affect our level of revenue and results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax-specific causal effect remains unresolved, but this is no longer solely a forward-looking risk: the latest filing says the tax began in 2026 and reports substantial post-effective-date deterioration. Management attributes the contraction more broadly to the retail remittance market and LAC corridor, so the record cannot isolate the tax. Nevertheless, projecting from FY2025 with growth rates of negative 3% to positive 5% omits current declines reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate owner earnings for the first half and trailing twelve months of 2026; obtain cash-remittance volume, pricing, channel migration and contribution-margin data before and after the tax became effective; isolate tax effects from immigration, corridor and competitive effects, then rerun the scenario path.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved legal claims may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured settlement, fine or defense payment reduces OE or becomes a liability deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Although there can be no assurance as to the ultimate disposition of these matters, it is the opinion of the Company’s management, based upon the information available at this time and the stage of the proceedings, that it is not possible to determine the probability of loss or estimate of damages, and therefore, the Company has not established a reserve for any of these proceedings.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved contingent possibility, not a demonstrated omitted liability. No reserve or estimable loss is filed, and management states that it cannot determine probability or damages while also expressing the view that proceedings should not be materially adverse. Without a quantified exposure, there is no concrete basis to establish materiality or classify it as not material.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings, dockets and merger-related disclosures for quantified claims, settlement developments, regulatory penalties, indemnification and insurance coverage; add a bridge deduction or scenario cash outflow only when supported by case-specific evidence.
